description: A Responses stream that ends with response.failed (server_error) reaches the Messages client as message_start followed by a terminal error event (type api_error, the upstream's message). No content block and no message_stop follow, and the failure is not turned into a successful message.
source: core/internal/runtime/executor/codex_executor_terminal.go (terminal event conversion: case response.failed reads the upstream error body)
core/internal/translator/codex/claude/codex_claude_response.go (ConvertCodexResponseToClaude: no case for response.failed; case error and codexStreamErrorToClaudeError)
next/corpus/cases/anthropic-messages/openai-responses/stream-response-failed.json (same exchange through the Responses API-key upstream)

error.message: The model failed to generate a response.

exceptions.reason: Today's core puts its own local estimate of the input tokens in message_start; the new core has no tokenizer and sends 0 there, as Anthropic's message_start allows, until message_delta carries the upstream's count.
The new core's Codex extension asks the upstream only for gzip, which Go's HTTP client decodes itself; today's core also advertises deflate, br and zstd.

When the client names no session, both cores derive a prompt cache key from the conversation's start so every turn of it shares the upstream's prompt cache; today's core hashes its own session identity (client key and canonical content), the new core's Codex extension the account, the model and the first developer and user messages. The values differ; each core's is stable across a conversation.

When the client names no session, both cores derive a prompt cache key from the conversation's start so every turn of it shares the upstream's prompt cache; today's core hashes its own session identity (client key and canonical content), the new core's Codex extension the account, the model and the first developer and user messages. The values differ; each core's is stable across a conversation.

The new core sends the reasoning effort the client asked for (reasoning_effort, a Messages thinking budget's effort or a model-name suffix) whatever the model, and gives a translated request that names none the medium effort today's core gives it; today's core checks the effort against its model catalog and drops it for a model it does not list, such as gpt-test. The *-catalog-model cases and the codex-oauth cases show both cores sending it for a model today's core lists.
